title: Reason containing NUL (\u0000) makes the audit_logs insert fail deterministically while the override is applied
evidence: NormalizeReason only trims and counts runes (ops_override.go:115-119). encoding/json decodes "\u0000" into a Go string with a 0x00 byte; Auditor.Record (services/waitingroom/internal/adapter/postgres/audit.go:35-38) binds it to a TEXT column and Postgres rejects 0x00 ('invalid byte sequence for encoding UTF8: 0x00'). By D2 the override stays applied and the response is audit:"failed". So an ops user can choose to keep any override out of audit_logs. The ERROR log line still carries actor/action/subject/metadata, so the trail is not lost entirely, which is why this is minor. The web client also accepts control characters (apps/web/src/lib/ops-service.ts:350-354).
repro: PUT /v1/ops/events/{id}/admit-override with an ops token and body {"rate_per_sec":0,"reason":"abc\u0000"} -> 200 {paused:true, audit:"failed"}, no audit_logs row.
fix: Reject reasons that contain control characters (unicode.IsControl, at least NUL) in NormalizeReason (400 /problems/invalid-override, nothing applied) and mirror this in normalizeOverrideReason on the web. Add an AC-9 case.

title: Single-flight serialises waiters on DB errors: each waiter then runs its own 2 s query in turn
evidence: Each entry's mutex is held for the whole load (ops_handler.go:229-247). Errors other than not-found are not cached (e.fill=false, line 245). When Postgres is slow or down (spec §5 'Postgres overloaded during a sale'), N queued requests for one event run N loads one after another, each up to opsLoadTimeout. The k-th waiter answers after about k×2 s, and the overloaded DB keeps getting a query every 2 s per waiter instead of at most one per TTL. Waiting on e.mu.Lock also ignores the request context. The impact is small because few clients poll one event (ops 2 s, organizer 4 s, gateway 10 rps per user).
repro: Stub OpsInventoryReader to sleep 2 s and return an error; fire 5 concurrent GETs: 5 loader calls in sequence, the last response after about 10 s.
fix: Briefly cache the error too (for example 1 s, or until the in-flight load finishes, then share its result with the waiters), or use singleflight.Group, which shares one result, error included, with all current waiters. Make the wait context-aware.

title: generated_at truncated to whole seconds on top of a 2 s cache makes the war room's oldest-source age reach the 5 s stale threshold
evidence: Inventory and sales format filledAt with time.RFC3339 (lines 117, 174), which drops up to 999 ms. The web takes the OLDEST generated_at among the sources (apps/web/src/lib/ops-service.ts:287-290) and marks data stale above STALE_AFTER_MS=5000. The worst-case age before the next poll is about cache age (<2 s) + truncation (<1 s) + poll interval (2 s) + RTT, so the stale warning can flicker on healthy data. Waitingroom already uses RFC3339Nano.
repro: Poll with the cache filled just after a second boundary; the age right before the next refresh approaches 5 s.
fix: Format with time.RFC3339Nano (or millisecond precision) in both ticketing handlers.

title: Write result fails open on audit status: a missing or unknown `audit` value is shown as recorded
evidence: `audit: w.audit === "failed" ? "failed" : "recorded"`. A malformed or proxied 200 without `audit` hides the 'Đã áp dụng nhưng chưa ghi được nhật ký kiểm toán' warning.
repro: Mock PUT 200 with body {override:{active:true,rate_per_sec:0},paused:true}: the UI shows success with no audit warning.
fix: Map only the exact value "recorded" to recorded, and treat anything else as "failed".

title: Expired session during a write shows 'Chưa gửi được lệnh / Thử lại' instead of sending the user to login
evidence: sendOverride rethrows ApiError(AUTH_REQUIRED) (ops-service.ts:399). errorCode() returns 'AUTH_REQUIRED', which ErrorOutcome does not handle, so it falls through to the generic retry alert. Also, a 401 response is mapped to FORBIDDEN (ops-service.ts:404) and shows 'Không có quyền' for what is an authentication failure. RoleGuard may redirect once useAuth sees the cleared session, but the control panel itself gives a misleading message and a retry button.
repro: Expire the refresh token, then click 'Ghi đè admit rate'.
fix: Handle AUTH_REQUIRED and 401 explicitly: show a 'phiên đăng nhập đã hết' message, or trigger the same login redirect as reads (OpsServiceError(401)).

title: Variadic Routes trades a compile-time guarantee for a runtime fail-closed one, and leaves a contradictory doc comment
evidence: The signature changed from Routes(mux, idempotency) to Routes(mux, idempotencyMW ...). A caller that forgets the middleware now compiles, and every write route answers 503 (idempotencyUnavailable, handler.go:216-221). That is safe (fail-closed) and the only production caller passes it (cmd/server/main.go:148), so no write route is left without idempotency. The old comment at line 87-88 ('BAT BUOC ... khong cho phep dang ky route ghi ma khong truyen') still sits above the new one and contradicts it.
fix: Remove the stale comment. Optionally keep the non-variadic signature and have the read-only ops tests pass a no-op middleware, as check_in_test.go does.

title: Role check trusts X-Identity-Role while the ai-worker port is published on all interfaces (pre-existing exposure)
evidence: deploy/compose/docker-compose.yml:249 publishes 8090 on 0.0.0.0, unlike waitingroom and ticketing (127.0.0.1). Anyone who reaches :8090 can send X-Identity-Role: ops. There is no new data exposure: the unauthenticated /admin/mode on the same port already returns a superset, and POST /admin/mode/{mode} is worse. Recorded so the header-trust model is not assumed to be safe for future ops write endpoints on ai-worker.
fix: Out of scope for this PR: bind 8090 to 127.0.0.1 in compose, as the other services do (follow-up debt).

title: Applied test change goes beyond the approved TCR row ('metadata text only')
evidence: tcr-applied.md says it itself: the file had no metadata assertion. Two sample-label assertions became 'no Dữ liệu mẫu' + badge 'Realtime (≤ 5s)'. The new assertions are not weaker (one negative check, one positive check), but the change was not what the human approved.
fix: Get human confirmation of this TCR deviation in the sign-off record. No code change needed.
